newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU prepares would-be members for disappointment.
newsitem.headline: EU prepares would-be members for disappointment.

text.p: East European countries should not read too much into being left out of the first round of European Union membership negotiations, the man charged with preparing the EU's expansion said on Tuesday.

Fearful of a backlash of public resentment in the countries having the greatest difficulty in distancing themselves from their Soviet past, External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek said different starting dates would not amount to discrimination or exclusion.
"There should not be a difference between ins and outs, but between ins and pre-ins," Van den Broek told reporters.

It was his second public statement in a week aimed at preparing eastern countries for possible disappointment when the European Commission publishes its recommendations to EU governments on July 16 on the applicants' readiness to join.
Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia, Slovenia, Estonia, Lithuania, Latvia, Bulgaria and Romania have all applied for membership of the wealthy western bloc.

Van den Broek stressed that the executive had not reached a final view on whether negotiations should begin with everyone at the same time, or just the best prepared, and that the final decision would lie with EU governments, who expect to decide by year end.
But he said he was reacting to heavy lobbying from some of the countries concerned and countries within the EU against differentiating between the applicants.

He said he was aware that public sensitivity in the eastern countries could be heightened by the fact that some of them face certain rejection when on July 8-9 the NATO military alliance invites a small number of former eastern foes from a list of 12 to begin entry talks.
But he said that could not influence the Commission's stance.
"Joining a political, military organisation NATO is something different to joining a political, economic and monetary union called the EU," he said.

Van den Broek said the Commission would only unveil its assessments on the 10 membership bids in Strasbourg on July 16 if the EU concluded on time at its June 16-17 Amsterdam Summit the inter-governmental conference aimed at overhauling the bloc for the day it has up to 12 new members.

In submitting its views the Commission would be outlining its vision for the EU next century, he said, pointing out that EU expansion would mean radically overhauling policy in areas from finances to agriculture.
He said that in outlining proposals for financing the expansion, the Commission would not propose increasing the ceiling on the EU's own resources -- the amount each member pays to the EU budget.

He said the Commission's main concern was with the applicants' ability to bring their legislation into line with the pages and pages of legislation in force in the bloc and then go on to implement that legislation.
